back: A field in one table that is the primary key of another table, used to link related records.
A database of two or more tables linked by matching values in primary and foreign key fields.
One record in table A links to many in table B; each B record links to one A record. The foreign key goes in B (the many side).
Add a link (junction) table holding the primary keys of both tables as foreign keys; it creates two one-to-many relationships.
A primary key made of two or more fields whose combined values are unique, e.g. (LearnerID, ClubID) in a link table.
Every foreign key value must match an existing primary key value in the linked table.

front: Crow's foot notation in an ERD
back: Entities are rectangles joined by lines; a plain end means one, a three-pronged (crow's foot) end means many.
Flat-file: one table. Hierarchical: tree, one parent each. Network: graph, several parents. Relational: tables linked by keys.
Importing brings data into a database from another source (e.g. CSV or spreadsheet); exporting sends data out in such a format.
